comparisons.peer_topic: On-Premises Edge AI and Computing Platforms
comparisons.peer_summary: The company develops high-performance, AI-enabled compute platforms using Intel Xeon, Core, and Atom processors for industries like retail and healthcare, delivering edge-optimized platforms to reduce operational complexity and enable faster data processing at the edge.
comparisons.comparison: Both AMD and Intel highlight the expansion of their AI portfolios specifically targeting edge and embedded systems, utilizing their respective semiconductor architectures. AMD expanded its 'adaptive computing portfolio' with Versal Series Gen 2 devices to accelerate 'AI-driven embedded systems,' while Intel developed 'high-performance, AI-enabled compute platforms' for 'on-premises edge' applications across industries like retail and healthcare. Both disclosures focus on delivering specialized silicon solutions that integrate AI capabilities directly into end-user environments, distinct from pure cloud data center acceleration.

sentences.text: We expanded our adaptive computing portfolio with differentiated solutions with the launch of the new Versal™ Series Gen 2 devices, including the new Versal AI Edge Series Gen 2 and Versal Prime Series Gen 2 adaptive SoCs, which bring preprocessing, AI inference, and postprocessing together in a single device for end-to-end acceleration of AI-driven embedded systems.

We develop high-performance, AI-enabled compute platforms that solve for technology and business use cases that scale across several industries, such as retail, education, manufacturing, energy, healthcare, and medical.

We deliver edge-optimized AI-enabled platforms for edge applications based on our Intel Xeon, Intel Core, and Intel Atom® processor portfolio, which reduces operational complexity for our customers and helps our customers create, store, and process data at the edge so they can analyze it faster and act on it sooner.
